authoritative_source: OpenFlights routes (ODbL) + OurAirports (Public Domain) + GeoNames (CC BY 4.0)
connectivity_density: 16,701 direct corridors over 2,522 air-connected cities; mean degree 13.2
family_intent: MEASURED in en, de and fr
serp_evidence: rome2rio holds 1,850,129 organic keywords on exactly this model, 589,488 in positions 1 to 3
commercial_value: HIGH, a traveller on a corridor is an eSIM buyer
utility_gate: graph edge required; both endpoints above a population floor; at least 3 statable facts; one page per unordered pair
why_each_cell_is_unique: Distance, the airports that serve the corridor, the number of independent operators evidencing it, and for one-transfer pairs the viable hubs and the detour each adds. All computed per pair from the graph.

authoritative_source: Wikidata P197 adjacent station (CC0 1.0)
connectivity_density: 280,733 adjacency statements exist globally; per-country fetch in progress
family_intent: MEASURED in de ("berlin hamburg zug" is the canonical form)
utility_gate: same as air, plus a bounded path length through the station graph
estimated_legitimate_capacity: NOT YET MEASURED. Rail connects far more European city pairs than air and at shorter distances air does not serve, so this is the largest single unknown in the plan.
why_each_cell_is_unique: The station sequence, the line, the number of intermediate stops and the distance differ per pair.

authoritative_source: OurAirports (Public Domain) + GeoNames (CC BY 4.0)
connectivity_density: 3,354 access relations, one per airport with a resolvable city
family_intent: MEASURED, "heathrow to london" 1,300 and "heathrow to paddington" 1,000
commercial_value: HIGH, arrival is when connectivity is bought
utility_gate: airport within 60km of the city; city above a population floor
why_each_cell_is_unique: The airport to city distance, the IATA code and the airport class. Ground transport operators and fares are NOT stated because no licensed source for them is on disk.

authoritative_source: OurAirports (Public Domain)
serp_evidence: an own distinct intent, not a flight pair
utility_gate: both airports serving one metro area and a real surface connection
why_each_cell_is_unique: Inter-airport distance and the surface options between two specific terminals.
evidence_status: MEASURED intent, NOT built. Found during this research and not previously modelled.

authoritative_source: each government foreign ministry; UK FCDO via the gov.uk content API under OGL v3 is captured
connectivity_density: every nationality by every destination has a policy, so density is 1
avg_unique_facts_per_cell: 4, the requirement class, passport validity months, blank pages and the authority
family_intent: MEASURED, 107 rows and about 90 destinations for US citizens alone at a 200 floor
serp_evidence: head terms 3,600 down to 200 across destinations
commercial_value: VERY HIGH, directly adjacent to the purchase
duplicate_risk: MEDIUM, many destinations share one policy, so identical policy clusters must roll up
utility_gate: an authoritative source per cell, a review date, and no legal guarantee
estimated_legitimate_capacity: 226 per nationality captured. The bound is the number of nationalities for which an authoritative source exists, NOT 200 x 226.
why_each_cell_is_unique: A different legal requirement: a US citizen needs an e-visa for India, an ETA for the UK and nothing for Mexico. That is a different answer, not a template.
evidence_status: MEASURED and in capture for GB.

authoritative_source: company registers, varying licences
utility_gate: a sourced, cell-specific fact set; a cell whose only difference is the name is rejected
why_each_cell_is_unique: Only if the page states registry facts for that company at that location: incorporation date, filing status, officers. Where it would only restate a name and an address it is a directory listing and is rejected.
evidence_status: NOT MEASURED. No licensed register on disk.

authoritative_source: salary and vacancy sources, mostly licensed
utility_gate: a sourced, cell-specific fact set; a cell whose only difference is the name is rejected
why_each_cell_is_unique: Only if a measured local salary distribution or vacancy count exists for that profession in that city. Livdar already holds salary data for a limited set; without it the cell is a city name swap and is rejected.
evidence_status: PARTLY MEASURED. The existing work surface finals 3,921, which is the honest size at current data.

authoritative_source: university prospectuses, no open licence
utility_gate: a sourced, cell-specific fact set; a cell whose only difference is the name is rejected
why_each_cell_is_unique: Only if the page states course-level facts: duration, entry requirements, fees, language of instruction. A university name plus a course name is not a page.

authoritative_source: national health registers, varying licences
utility_gate: a sourced, cell-specific fact set; a cell whose only difference is the name is rejected
why_each_cell_is_unique: Only where waiting times, service availability or accreditation differ per hospital and service. In most countries that data is not open.

authoritative_source: event feeds, mostly licensed
utility_gate: a sourced, cell-specific fact set; a cell whose only difference is the name is rejected
why_each_cell_is_unique: Each date genuinely differs, but a page per venue per date is the temporal trap: most dates have no event and the page would be empty. Only dates with a sourced event qualify.
evidence_status: PARTLY MEASURED. events surface finals 6,680 per family.

authoritative_source: government tax authorities
utility_gate: a sourced, cell-specific fact set; a cell whose only difference is the name is rejected
why_each_cell_is_unique: Only if the page states the actual rates, thresholds and treaty position for that status in that country. That is real and differs per cell, but it is advice-adjacent and needs a disclaimer discipline at least as strict as visa.

authoritative_source: land registries and rent indices, varying licences
utility_gate: a sourced, cell-specific fact set; a cell whose only difference is the name is rejected
why_each_cell_is_unique: Only where a measured price or rent index exists for that area. Livdar holds rent data for a limited set, which finals 5,202.

authoritative_source: NASA POWER normals already on disk
utility_gate: a sourced, cell-specific fact set; a cell whose only difference is the name is rejected
why_each_cell_is_unique: A different measured temperature, rainfall and daylight figure per city and month. Real, and already built as weather.city-month at 22,927.

authoritative_source: OSM and GeoNames places already on disk, plus the measured per-language demand
estimated_valid_entity_count_A: 3,979 destination tokens recovered from the measured keywords
connectivity_density: measured per language rather than assumed: 382 destinations carry demand in two or more source languages and 171 in three or more
legitimate_connected_cells: roughly 8,000 to 12,000 on the measured two-language-or-more rule
avg_unique_facts_per_cell: the attraction list differs by source language because the audience differs: a Turkish reader asking about Bakü wants different emphasis from a Swede asking about Prague
serp_evidence: 12,421 open-SERP rows banked, 8,011 of them in this family across 11 languages carrying 13.5 million monthly searches
duplicate_risk: MEDIUM. The translation-clone trap is exactly here and the own-language rule is what holds it back
utility_gate: a page may exist in a language only where that language shows measured demand for that destination. Not a fan-out.
why_each_cell_is_unique: each cell is a different audience asking about the same place, and only exists where that audience was measured

authoritative_source: the measured keywords; the itinerary content itself is not yet sourced
estimated_valid_entity_count_A: 72 destinations clear the floor in English
connectivity_density: 33 of 72 destinations appear at more than one duration, and each duration carries its own parent topic
avg_unique_facts_per_cell: a two-day itinerary and a ten-day itinerary are genuinely different content, not one page with a variable swapped in
family_intent: PROVEN in 4 languages independently (en, de, pl, it)
serp_evidence: 323 English rows at a median CPC far above the rest of the inventory, 68 at 1.00 USD or more; 76 Italian rows in one band alone; 14 Polish rows at KD 0; Italian even reaches "in mezza giornata"
commercial_value: HIGH. median CPC 0.20 and a maximum of 1.40 USD
duplicate_risk: LOW, because the duration materially changes the answer
utility_gate: the page must contain a real day-by-day plan. Without ordered, routed content this is a thin page and must not be built.
stage: STAGE 2, needs an itinerary data model first
why_each_cell_is_unique: the ordering and selection of what fits in N days is the content, and it differs for every N

authoritative_source: a handset capability table, which does not exist as an open dataset and must be built
estimated_valid_entity_count_A: a few thousand handset models in the market
estimated_valid_entity_count_B: capability is a small enumeration, so B is not really an axis
connectivity_density: every model has exactly one answer, so density is 1
avg_unique_facts_per_cell: the fact per cell is the capability itself plus the generation it arrived in and the profile count
serp_evidence: 176 rows, 83 at a CPC of 3.00 USD or more, a maximum of 55.00 USD, and almost the entire tail at KD 0 or 1
duplicate_risk: LOW if the capability fact is real, TOTAL if it is guessed
utility_gate: a wrong answer on a KD 0 page with a 30 USD CPC is worse than no page. No capability table, no pages.
stage: STAGE 1 commercially, STAGE 0 on data: the table has to be built first
why_each_cell_is_unique: each model either carries an eSIM or does not, and that single fact is the whole answer the reader wants

authoritative_source: a per-country carrier list, researchable but not open
avg_unique_facts_per_cell: which local carriers sell eSIM, whether a visitor can activate one, and what a traveller should do instead where they cannot
serp_evidence: ten rows measured at KD 0 to 7 (Bangladesh, Vietnam, Philippines, India, Japan, Israel, Mexico, Nepal) with CPC up to 1.20 USD
commercial_value: HIGH and directly on Livdar product
utility_gate: overlaps the destination axis, so it belongs on country pages Livdar already has rather than as a new tree
why_each_cell_is_unique: each country has a different carrier set and a different answer for a visiting traveller

authoritative_source: a carrier capability table per market
estimated_valid_entity_count_A: a few hundred carriers across Livdar markets
avg_unique_facts_per_cell: whether the carrier issues eSIM profiles, how, and what it costs to switch
serp_evidence: eleven rows measured, CPC 1.80 to 25.00 USD, KD 0 to 10
utility_gate: carrier names are brands. Each page must carry a factual capability statement and nothing that reads as an endorsement or a comparison Livdar cannot support.
why_each_cell_is_unique: each carrier has a different answer and a different switching procedure

authoritative_source: the graph already built: 7,312 nodes and 21,480 edges from OurAirports, OpenFlights and Wikidata rail
estimated_valid_entity_count_A: 14,805 air pairs and 46,856 rail pairs already materialised
estimated_valid_entity_count_B: air, rail, road, ferry, airport transfer
connectivity_density: measured, not assumed: 346 of 500 English distance rows and 139 of 500 English route rows name two real places
legitimate_connected_cells: the 61,661 already built, because a pair page should answer every mode at once rather than split by mode
avg_unique_facts_per_cell: distance, modes, route options, transfers, nearest stations and airports, operators where the source permits
serp_evidence: 1,000 English rows banked at a median KD 0 and 891 at KD 10 or below; airport access and short intercity pairs carry CPC up to 1.20 USD
commercial_value: MEDIUM to HIGH on airport access
duplicate_risk: LOW, measured: highest shingle Jaccard 0.672 across 59,594 comparisons, zero pairs at 0.80 or above
utility_gate: mode is NOT a separate axis. The parent topics show distance and route are one canonical intent, so one page per pair answers all modes. Splitting by mode would manufacture duplicates.
estimated_legitimate_capacity: 61,661 already built, more as the graph grows
why_each_cell_is_unique: each pair is a different journey with different distance, modes, operators and transfer points
evidence_status: MEASURED 2026-10-07. REFUTED in German: only 2 of 500 rows name two places, so this axis must NOT be fanned out across languages without a probe per language.

authoritative_source: OpenStreetMap route=ferry relations (ODbL 1.0), the same licence the POI corpus uses
estimated_valid_entity_count_A: thousands of ferry terminals in OSM
connectivity_density: a ferry route is an explicit OSM relation, so connectivity is stated rather than inferred
legitimate_connected_cells: the routes OSM actually records, which is thousands not millions
avg_unique_facts_per_cell: crossing distance, duration where the relation states it, the operator, the vehicle policy, the terminals at each end
serp_evidence: 219 English rows at a floor of 300 on enterable SERPs, 65 of 72 recorded at KD 10 or below
commercial_value: HIGHEST of the three pair modes: median CPC above air and rail, head at 3.00 USD
duplicate_risk: LOW, each crossing is a different journey
utility_gate: one page per crossing naming both directions, the same rule the air and rail pairs use
stage: STAGE 1, buildable now and the cheapest new mode
why_each_cell_is_unique: each crossing has its own terminals, operator, duration and vehicle rules

authoritative_source: OSM amenity=parking polygons with capacity and fee tags (ODbL), coverage NOT yet checked
estimated_valid_entity_count_A: airports 4,133 already in the register, plus stations, temples, castles, parks, aquariums, zoos, theme parks, stadiums and malls already held as POI
connectivity_density: every entity either has car parking or does not
legitimate_connected_cells: the entities that actually have a car park with recorded capacity
avg_unique_facts_per_cell: how many spaces, the fee structure, whether booking is possible, walking distance to the entrance
serp_evidence: English airport parking 29,000 at KD 0; 275 of 300 English rows name an airport; Japanese reaches deep into attractions with dozens at KD 0
commercial_value: HIGH. English median CPC 1.00 with 155 of 300 rows at 1.00 or more
duplicate_risk: LOW if the capacity fact is real
utility_gate: no capacity data, no page. A guessed space count on a commercial query is worse than no page.
stage: STAGE 2: demand proven, source coverage unverified
why_each_cell_is_unique: each car park has its own capacity, price and walking distance

authoritative_source: OSM site=piste and landuse=winter_sports (ODbL), plus the terrain data the peak layer already uses
estimated_valid_entity_count_A: roughly two thousand named ski areas worldwide
legitimate_connected_cells: the areas with a recorded lift system
avg_unique_facts_per_cell: elevation, vertical drop, lift and run counts, season dates, which pass covers it
serp_evidence: 162 English rows at a floor of 500, only two above KD 40 and both generic
commercial_value: STRONG. CPC 0.45 to 1.20 with outliers at 4.00 and 5.00
utility_gate: the entity page only. The snow report is live state and is refused: real demand, but fabricating conditions is forbidden and a stale report is worse than none.
why_each_cell_is_unique: each area has its own terrain, lift system and season
evidence_status: MEASURED 2026-10-07. The snow-report half REFUSED on principle.

authoritative_source: no licensed source identified
estimated_valid_entity_count_A: regions and provinces in the eleven markets
avg_unique_facts_per_cell: which markets and fairs are on in this region this weekend
family_intent: PROVEN in German and Spanish as a by-product of refuting the market category
serp_evidence: maerkte und feste heute in der naehe 3,200, maerkte in der naehe 3,000, maerkte und feste in berlin heute dieses wochenende 1,300, mercados en asturias este fin de semana 1,100, ferias y mercados en gipuzkoa hoy 600
duplicate_risk: HIGH, because a weekend list is near-duplicate across weeks unless the events differ
utility_gate: this is LIVE EVENT data. Livdar has no licensed source for it and must not invent one.
why_each_cell_is_unique: each weekend in each region has a different set of events, IF the data exists
